No implementation, naive or otherwise, reads that as a continuation, because every candidate rule requires whitespace before the underscore. The stated interesting failure mode ('an implementation that strips continuations in a pre-pass over raw text will happily produce a working import of kernel32') is therefore unreachable, and all this measures is an unterminated string literal - already covered three times over. Fix by writing "kern _ / el32" so a space precedes the underscore, which is what continuation-basics/cont-inside-string-literal does correctly. That fact is already measured twice (separator-basics/sep-rem-without-colon, separator-vs-label/rem-without-colon), and because the snippet dies before the underscore matters, the continuation question it exists to ask is unmeasurable. HARNESS HAZARD. separator-in-control-flow/label-in-the-middle-of-a-line jumps backwards to a label that precedes its own GoTo with no exit condition: if the answer is 'legal', the program prints B and loops forever. Its why says '(Note this snippet loops forever if legal -- it is a compile-only probe.)', but the case schema has no compile-only field, so a runner that executes the corpus hangs there and every other legal case in the area gets attributed a timeout. The code above is the SUGGESTED REPLACEMENT, not the offending snippet: it asks the identical question (may a name-colon be a label when it is not first on the physical line) with a guard variable so it terminates, printing A B B AFTER if legal. The offending original is separator-in-control-flow/label-in-the-middle-of-a-line, two lines: 'Debug.Print "A" : Retry: Debug.Print "B"' followed by 'GoTo Retry'. separator-in-control-flow/label-then-colon-joined-goto-target already uses the guard pattern, so the fix is in-house.

SCHEMA VIOLATION, three cases. The code field is specified as one string per physical line, but whitespace-and-eol-edges/cr-only-line-endings embeds bare CR inside a single element, /lf-only-line-endings embeds bare LF, and /mixed-crlf-and-lf embeds an LF inside element two. What reaches vb6.exe then depends entirely on how the harness joins and whether it normalises: a harness that splits on any newline, or writes through a text-mode writer that translates LF to CRLF, silently converts all three into the ordinary CRLF case and reports a confident 'legal' that measures nothing. If line endings are to be measured they need a field that says so, not an escape smuggled through a field documented as line-per-element.  [snippet quoted verbatim from whitespace-and-eol-edges.json / cr-only-line-endings]

ENCODING-DEPENDENT. whitespace-and-eol-edges/nbsp-as-indentation puts U+00A0 at the start of a line and reasons that 'this byte is a printable character in the ANSI codepage'. That holds only if the file is written as Windows-1252 (one byte, 0xA0). Written as UTF-8 - the normal default - vb6.exe sees two bytes, 0xC2 0xA0: still illegal, but for a different reason, so the recorded fact would be wrong even though the prediction is right. The same exposure applies to any non-ASCII byte in the corpus. State the required file encoding, or restrict the case to ASCII controls the way vertical-tab-between-tokens and form-feed-as-page-break-line do.  [snippet quoted verbatim from whitespace-and-eol-edges.json / nbsp-as-indentation]

HARNESS COLLISION, three cases. separator-with-declarations/attribute-then-option, /attribute-colon-option and /attribute-value-continued each write an explicit Attribute VB_Name = "Mod1" line into the module body. A .bas file exported or generated by the toolchain already begins with its own Attribute VB_Name for the module being saved, so unless the harness knows to strip its header for these three, vb6.exe sees a duplicate or conflicting attribute and the result is illegal for a reason with nothing to do with colons or continuations. That turns attribute-then-option ('legal') into a false negative and makes attribute-colon-option ('illegal') true for the wrong reason.  [snippet quoted verbatim from separator-with-declarations.json / attribute-then-option]

CONFOUNDED BY UNSTATED HARNESS POLICY. continuation-illegal/no-space-before-underscore-after-identifier relies on ab_ lexing as a fresh, never-declared Variant - outcome (b) in its own why. That outcome exists only if the enclosing module has no Option Explicit. Several module-scope cases elsewhere in the corpus open with Option Explicit, so the statement-scope wrapper is doing something unstated; if it ever adds Option Explicit, this case reports 'illegal' for an undeclared variable rather than for anything to do with underscores. The same exposure covers separator-with-declarations/deftype-colon-joined (needs implicit k and p) continuation-vs-identifier/lone-continuation-line-between-statements, and gap-fill/named-argument-colon-and-equals-split (where Msg is the callee's parameter name and is undeclared in Main, so under an Option Explicit wrapper the module fails on the name rather than on the split ':=' it exists to probe). Pin the wrapper's Option Explicit policy in the notes and make every case that depends on it say so.  [snippet quoted verbatim from continuation-illegal.json / no-space-before-underscore-after-identifier]

HARNESS CONTRACT, unstated. Module-scope cases in this area disagree about the entry point: most use Sub Main (continuation-basics/cont-signature-between-params, most of separator-with-declarations), separator-vs-label and continuation-in-strings-comments use Sub Test, and every whitespace-and-eol-edges module uses Sub S - with /form-feed-as-page-break-line defining Sub S and Sub T and no Main at all. If the harness only compiles, this is harmless; if it links or runs, the no-Main cases fail for a reason unrelated to whitespace. Either fix on one convention or record in the notes that module cases are compile-only.  [snippet quoted verbatim from whitespace-and-eol-edges.json / form-feed-as-page-break-line]

METADATA DEFECT - not the snippet quoted, which is a sound control case and appears only because this finding needs a code field. Seven of the eleven files omit the top-level count field entirely: continuation-illegal, continuation-vs-identifier, gap-fill, separator-and-continuation-together, separator-basics, separator-vs-label, separator-with-declarations. gap-fill additionally ships an empty notes field, where every other file uses notes to record load-bearing whitespace and harness caveats - and gap-fill has the most whitespace-critical content in the area (a TAB after Rem, a TAB-then-space before an underscore, a 1106-character physical line that any JSON reformatter would be tempted to wrap). The area field is also inconsistent in kind: four files give prose ('colon as a statement separator'), four give a slug path ('continuation-and-separator/gap-fill'), so the field cannot be grouped on. 322 cases across eleven files in two metadata shapes will not aggregate cleanly.  [snippet quoted verbatim from continuation-illegal.json / baseline-well-formed-continuation]

NON-MINIMAL, and its own why says so. gap-fill/with-block-colon-tight-against-dot-and-end fires two distinct lexer hazards in one line - ':.' (separator immediately followed by a leading-dot member access) and ':End' (where E is a hex digit that the grammar's FRX_OFFSET token could swallow). Both are real and both deserve a case, but a rejection here cannot say which one caused it, which is exactly what the corpus needs to know. It also drags in a Private Type declaration purely to have something with a dotted member, where separator-basics/sep-with-block-one-line reaches the same shape with the intrinsic Err object and no declaration at all. Split into 'With Err:.Number ...' and '... :End With' as two cases.  [snippet quoted verbatim from gap-fill.json / with-block-colon-tight-against-dot-and-end]

NON-MINIMAL, mildly. gap-fill/print-tab-and-spc-with-colon-joined-statements probes Tab() and Spc() in the same snippet. They are separate Print-only pseudo-functions handled by the same special output-list rule, so one of them is enough to test whether that rule terminates at a colon; carrying both means a failure needs a second run to localise. notes: Provenance and quality audit of the eleven case files in this directory (322 cases total; gap-fill.json landed while this audit was in progress and is covered). Clean-room: produced by reading only the sibling JSON files here, the repo grammar IDE/HexIDE.Runtime/Interpreter/Grammar/VB6.g4, and the local VBA-Docs corpus for language facts. No GPL-licensed VB6 grammar or test suite was consulted, searched for, or recalled; no sibling file was modified or deleted. Every case below is expect:'unsure' because each flags a defect in a sibling case rather than asserting a fact about vb6.exe; the code array reproduces the offending snippet verbatim, whitespace preserved, so a runner can still execute it, and the why names the offending id. HEADLINE: at least 31 distinct questions are asked more than once, accounting for roughly 90 of the 285 cases - and SEVEN of those duplicate groups carry CONTRADICTORY predictions, so one compiler run will score the same fact both right and wrong. Those seven (dup-trailing-whitespace-after-underscore, dup-tab-before-underscore, dup-empty-continuation-line, dup-continuation-after-member-dot, dup-colon-immediately-after-then, dup-identifier-ending-in-underscore, dup-label-after-a-colon-mid-line) are the highest-value fix, because they are the only ones that can actively corrupt the recorded result rather than merely waste a run. The heaviest structural overlaps are separator-basics against separator-vs-label and separator-basics against separator-in-control-flow (roughly eight pairs each, several byte-identical), and the four continuation files against each other, where four probes - comment-after-underscore, no-space-before-underscore, colon-then-continuation, single-line-if-colon-tail - each appear four times. THREE FINDINGS WOULD PRODUCE FALSE 'ILLEGAL' RESULTS: declare-continuation-inside-lib-string (the underscore is not preceded by a space, so the continuation it claims to test cannot fire and only an unterminated string is measured); rem-after-statement-without-colon (dies at Rem before the underscore is reached); and the Attribute VB_Name trio, which will likely collide with a harness-generated .bas header. THREE MORE WOULD PRODUCE A CONFIDENT ANSWER THAT MEASURES NOTHING: the embedded-newline trio in whitespace-and-eol-edges, which a normalising harness silently converts into the ordinary CRLF case; nbsp-as-indentation, right answer for the wrong reason unless the file is written as Windows-1252; and no-space-before-underscore-after-identifier, which flips on an unstated Option Explicit policy. ONE OPERATIONAL HAZARD: label-in-the-middle-of-a-line runs forever if the answer is 'legal', and a run-and-capture harness will read that as a timeout across the whole area. NOT A DEFECT BUT WORTH PROTECTING: whitespace is load-bearing and invisible in at least a dozen cases - trailing spaces and tabs after an underscore, a lone space-underscore line, tabs standing in for spaces, and the VT/FF/NBSP characters in whitespace-and-eol-edges. Any reformat, right-trim, or re-encode of these files destroys the measurement without visibly changing the JSON. gap-fill.json deserves separate mention: it is the only file whose whys check for prior art by name before adding a case, and most of what it adds is genuinely new (time and date literals whose colons are not separators, the 24-vs-25 consecutive-continuation cap, a physical line over 1023 characters as the complement to whitespace-and-eol-edges/logical-line-over-1023-chars, End If / End Select / Exit For split by a continuation, bracketed identifiers containing a colon, a continuation between & and the H of a hex literal). Its four findings here are near-misses, not blind duplication. The corpus is otherwise strong: the whys are unusually honest about their own reasoning, 'unsure' is used where it genuinely belongs rather than as a hedge, and most legal cases print a discriminating literal so acceptance can be told apart from correct execution. The problems here are almost entirely the result of ten files being authored against overlapping briefs with no cross-file dedup pass, not of weak individual cases.
